In the latest trading session, Microsoft (MSFT) closed at $525.18, marking a +1.48% move from the previous day. The stock's change was more than the S&P 500's daily gain of 0.66%. Elsewhere, the Dow gained 0.18%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq added 1.05%.

Heading into today, shares of the software maker had gained 3.57% over the past month, lagging the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 6.36% and outpacing the S&P 500's gain of 0.55%.

The upcoming earnings release of Microsoft will be of great interest to investors. The company's earnings per share (EPS) are projected to be $4.7, reflecting a 13.8% increase from the same quarter last year. In the meantime, our current consensus estimate forecasts the revenue to be $90.63 billion, indicating a 16.68% growth compared to the corresponding quarter of the prior year.

In terms of the entire fiscal year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates predict earnings of $19.62 per share and a revenue of $389.65 billion, indicating changes of +9.3% and +17.42%, respectively, from the former year.

It's also important for investors to be aware of any recent modifications to analyst estimates for Microsoft. Such recent modifications usually signify the changing landscape of near-term business trends. As a result, we can interpret positive estimate revisions as a good sign for the business outlook.

Empirical research indicates that these revisions in estimates have a direct correlation with impending stock price performance. To capitalize on this, we've crafted the Zacks Rank, a unique model that incorporates these estimate changes and offers a practical rating system.

The Zacks Rank system, stretching from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), has a noteworthy track record of outperforming, validated by third-party audits, with stocks rated #1 producing an average annual return of +25% since the year 1988. Within the past 30 days, our consensus EPS projection has moved 0.02% higher. Microsoft is currently a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Looking at its valuation, Microsoft is holding a Forward P/E ratio of 26.38. This signifies a premium in comparison to the average Forward P/E of 15.71 for its industry.

We can additionally observe that MSFT currently boasts a PEG ratio of 1.66. This metric is used similarly to the famous P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also takes into account the stock's expected earnings growth rate. The Computer - Software was holding an average PEG ratio of 1.45 at yesterday's closing price.

The Computer - Software industry is part of the Computer and Technology sector. This industry, currently bearing a Zacks Industry Rank of 103, finds itself in the top 42% echelons of all 250+ industries.

stocks market trading wall street equity -Shutterstock

(Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

The Nasdaq Composite hit a new peak on Monday to lead Wall Street's advance, driven by certain technology giants, as the 10-year yield crossed the 5.3% mark.

The tech-heavy index gained 1.1% to a fresh closing high of 27,477.31. The S&P 500 added 0.7% to settle at 7,773.95, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.2% to 51,267.90. Barring real estate, all sectors ended in the green, led by materials.

Shares of tech giants Nvidia (NVDA) and Microsoft (MSFT) were among the top gainers on the Dow, up 2.1% and 1.5%, respectively. Alphabet's (GOOGL) class A shares also advanced.

The 10-year Treasury yield was last up 3.4 basis points at 5.31%, having hit 5.349% earlier in the day. That was the highest level since April 3, 2002, CNBC reported.

The two-year rate was little changed.

"Treasury yields remain the principal near-term risk to stocks," Ivan Feinseth, chief market strategist at Tigress Financial Intelligence, said in a note. "Still, the fundamental backdrop remains supportive, with accelerating earnings growth, strong (artificial intelligence)-related capital investment, expanding semiconductor demand, increasing corporate buybacks and continued economic expansion."

In economic news, growth in the US services sector decelerated sequentially in September, Institute for Supply Management data showed, while an S&P Global (SPGI) report pointed to the fastest expansion in more than five years, with both surveys indicating inflationary pressures.

Last week, ISM and S&P surveys showed that the US manufacturing sector continued to expand last month amid robust demand and growth in employment, though inflationary pressures remained a key concern.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil was down 2.1% at $89.22 a barrel in Monday late-afternoon trade, while Brent dropped 2% to $100.22.

Oil flows in Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline were operating normally, following media reports that it had suffered a new attack, Bloomberg News reported Monday, citing unnamed sources.

In other company news, PTC (PTC) shares surged 34%, the top gainer on the S&P 500, after the engineering software provider agreed to be acquired by French conglomerate Schneider Electric in an all-cash deal valued at about $23.7 billion.

C.H. Robinson Worldwide (CHRW) agreed to acquire RXO (RXO) in a cash-and-stock deal worth roughly $5.8 billion to create a more than $25 billion third-party logistics provider. C.H. Robinson shares tumbled about 11%, while RXO soared nearly 23%.

PepsiCo (PEP) and Delta Air Lines (DAL) are scheduled to report their latest quarterly financial results later this week.

Spot gold edged down 0.1% to $4,138.10 per troy ounce, while silver climbed 1.6% to $61.41 per ounce.

Tech stocks were mixed late Monday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rising 0.7% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) shedding 0.3%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 0.3%.

In corporate news, Schneider Electric said Monday it is acquiring PTC (PTC) in an all-cash deal valued at $23.7 billion. Schneider said it will pay $205 per PTC share. PTC shares surged nearly 34%.

Meta Platforms (META) and Microsoft (MSFT) are reducing employees' use of Anthropic's Claude as they push their own AI tools, The Information reported. Meta shares were up 2.1%, and Microsoft rose 2.2%.

Strategy (MSTR) recorded an estimated $20.91 billion gain on digital assets in Q3, the company said in a Monday filing. Its shares rose 3.2%.

SpaceX (SPCX) shares are "cheap and getting cheaper," Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas said in a note. The shares have hovered around $150 per share since early August, and at $159, investors can take advantage of an opportunity to buy shares that, "while expensive on any trailing metric, look unusually cheap on the forward," Jonas said. Morgan Stanley maintained its overweight rating and $300 price target on the company. SpaceX shares jumped past 6%.

Nvidia's (NVDA) $20 billion licensing deal with Groq is the subject of a lawsuit alleging that Groq's board improperly sold the AI firm's core assets and top engineers, the Financial Times reported. The lawsuit, filed on Friday by Groq engineers and shareholders Benjamin Serebrin and Joshua Rubin, accuses the firm's board of not seeking to get the best price and structure for all shareholders, and not allowing some of them to vote on the deal, the report said. Nvidia shares were up 2.5%.

title: Melius Research upgrades Microsoft stock to Buy, $665 target
detail:
Melius Research upgrades Microsoft stock to Buy, $665 target
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stands before a screen that says "Age of AI" · Quartz · Dimas Ardian/Bloomberg via Getty Images
Cris Tolomia
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 10:31 AM MST
MSFT
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Melius Research upgraded Microsoft stock to Buy on Monday, setting a $665 price target, as the firm argued the company's software portfolio and cybersecurity business make it a compelling option for investors seeking lower-risk exposure to artificial intelligence, according to MarketWatch.

Ben Reitzes, the Melius Research analyst behind the call, wrote that Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and his leadership team will be viewed as the "adults in charge" as the dominant narrative around AI shifts toward safety concerns, according to MarketWatch. Reitzes noted that warnings from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and others about the potential dangers of AI have prompted investors to rethink how they approach the sector.

Microsoft's cybersecurity offerings have been a growing part of its business. The company launched MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, its first cybersecurity-focused AI model, alongside an agentic security platform called Project Perception. Microsoft last reported its cybersecurity revenue above $20 billion annually in 2023 and has not updated that figure since.

The AI safety debate has also drawn Microsoft into policy territory. The company posted a provisional code of conduct for its in-house AI models — branded as MAI — that bars the systems from assisting with weapons manufacturing, facilitating access to hazardous materials, or generating violent or sexually explicit content. Nadella said the company welcomes "the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right."

The upgrade comes after a strong stretch for Microsoft stock. The company posted a 37.5% gain in the third quarter, its best quarterly performance since 1998, lifting its market capitalization by $1 trillion. The rally was driven in large part by a single-day jump of 16% following an earnings report that showed cloud growth at its fastest pace in four years. Despite that run, Microsoft stock had returned only 6.1% on a year-to-date basis heading into the current quarter, well behind the Nasdaq 100's 20% advance over the same period.

Wall Street sentiment toward Microsoft has grown broadly positive. Among 72 analysts tracked by Bloomberg, all but three carry buy ratings on the stock, and not one recommends selling. Melius Research's upgrade adds to that consensus, framing Microsoft's maturity — in both its AI spending discipline and its security capabilities — as a competitive advantage in an environment where investors are growing more cautious about AI risk.

A weak U.S. jobs report, lofty Treasury yields near 5.3% and volatile energy and gold prices have put rate sensitive tech stocks like Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia back under the microscope. Some investors are pulling toward bonds. Others see potential mispricing in large growth names that move sharply when rate expectations shift. This article examines three stocks from our screener that appear especially exposed to this macro shock.

The three highlighted stocks are just a starting sample, since the full screen surfaced 31 more large-cap U.S. technology and growth companies with equally compelling rate sensitivity narratives that are not covered here. To go deeper, head straight into the Large-Cap U.S. Technology and Growth Stocks screener to identify, analyze, and prioritize the highest conviction ideas for your watchlist.

Microsoft (MSFT)

Microsoft is one of the clearest examples in this screener of a large U.S. technology group whose cloud and AI engine ties market sensitivity directly to rate expectations, and the quote below captures how that long-term growth story intersects with heavy infrastructure spending.

"Microsoft isn't spending $37.5 billion a quarter because Satya Nadella lost his mind. It's spending $37.5 billion a quarter because customer demand for Azure cloud computing is growing at 39% per year and the company literally cannot build servers fast enough."

What ultimately happens to profitability if a single underlying assumption behind that spending and demand curve shifts even slightly?

Microsoft is a global technology group whose software, cloud and AI platforms fit squarely into the large-cap U.S. growth theme, generating about US$140b from Productivity and Business Processes, US$138b from Intelligent Cloud and US$54b from More Personal Computing, with a market value near US$3.8t.

If that shift in assumptions is what keeps you watching Microsoft, read the full narrative for Microsoft to see how infrastructure, AI demand and rates could be decoupling.

Cloudflare (NET)

Cloudflare is one of the purest fits for this large-cap U.S. technology and growth screen. It is a cloud-based security and edge network platform that investors often treat as a long-duration asset whose value can swing hard when interest rate expectations reset.

Cloudflare runs a global cloud and edge network that secures and accelerates internet traffic for enterprises, with its reported Internet Telephone segment generating about US$2.5b in revenue, and the stock carrying a market value near US$124.3b.

Scotiabank sees Microsoft as a key player in the shift toward enterprise AI.

Wells Fargo recently raised its price target to $725 from $700 and added Microsoft to its Q4 'Tactical Ideas list,' citing its AI advantage and AI monetization opportunity.

Microsoft (MSFT) was in focus on Monday after Melius Research upgraded the stock to 'Buy' from 'Hold', saying concerns around AI risks could make companies such as Microsoft and cybersecurity providers increasingly important.

Scotiabank separately raised its price target on Microsoft to $615 from $510 while maintaining an 'Outperform' rating.

MSFT shares were trading 1.70% higher at the time of writing on Monday.

Melius Upgrades Microsoft To 'Buy'

According to TheFly, Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes upgraded Microsoft to 'Buy' from 'Hold' with a $665 price target.

The firm said Microsoft and cybersecurity companies could become increasingly important as AI leaders discuss the risks associated with the technology. Melius believes leaders such as Microsoft could benefit from AI fears, TheFly reported.

Melius also said enterprises are spending on a secure wrapper that can route models to the right task and secure AI agents.

Scotiabank Raises Microsoft Price Target

Separately, Scotiabank analyst Patrick Colville raised the firm's price target on Microsoft to $615 from $510 while maintaining an 'Outperform' rating, according to TheFly.

The firm named Microsoft among the enterprise software winners from OpenAI's recent business-to-business push. Scotiabank also said Microsoft is at the forefront of the enterprise AI revolution.

Analysts See Microsoft Benefiting From AI Monetization

Recently, Wells Fargo analyst Michael Turrin raised the firm's price target on Microsoft to $725 from $700 while maintaining an 'Overweight' rating and added the stock to its Q4 'Tactical Ideas list'.

Turrin cited Microsoft's AI advantage, the upcoming Ignite conference, and new segment reporting as key catalysts, according to TheFly.

Wells Fargo also said momentum was shifting back toward Microsoft among mega-cap technology companies as the company delivers on its AI monetization strategy alongside a balanced investment approach.

Azure Demand Supports AI Growth

Microsoft has said customer demand for Azure continues to exceed available capacity. In its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call, the company said it added another gigawatt of capacity and remained on track to roughly double its overall capacity in two years.
